unmapped_findings: Data for the Al-10 (Fe30Mn10Al1C) alloy in the 1050 °C/2 h solution-treated state — NOT this 1100 °C sample — are: UTS 830 ± 0 MPa, YS 642 ± 2 MPa, uniform elongation 72 ± 2.8%, total elongation 73.5 ± 1%, and Charpy impact toughness 237 ± 5 J at −40 °C (Table 2, row Al-10). These values belong to the 1050 °C state and must not be assigned to the 1100 °C sample.

The 1050 °C/2 h solution-treated Al-10 microstructure (Table 3, block b0047) is: single austenite phase, D_FCC-G/T = 29.7 ± 1.1 μm, twin-boundary fraction f_Tw = 53.2%, no ferrite (f_Bcc and D_Bcc not reported), κ-carbide diameter 1.0 ± 0.4 nm. These microstructural values correspond to the 1050 °C state, not to this 1100 °C sample.

For the present 1100 °C sample the paper reports only that the yield strength slightly decreases with increasing solution-treatment temperature relative to the 1050 °C values (Fig. 2d), attributed to increased grain size; no numeric tensile values are tabulated for the 1100 °C state.

For the 1100 °C Al-series solution treatment, work-hardening rate curves (Fig. 8d) retain the ordering 6Al highest → 12Al lowest; the stress-strain curves extend to noticeably larger true strain than at 1050 °C; σ_TS and σ_FS are reported as not varying significantly with C, Mn and Al after 1050 °C or 1100 °C treatment.

Density as a function of alloying content: ρ = 8.10 − 0.102C − 0.10Al − 0.01Mn g/cm³ (Eq. 3; C, Al, Mn in mass%), which predicts 6.6 g/cm³ for Fe30Mn11Al1.0C matching experiment; this is a general relation for the FeMnAlC series rather than a value specific to this sample (blocks b0063, b0081; figure_unlabelled_008).

General (not sample-specific) κ-carbide strengthening relations derived in the paper: σ_shear = α f^(1/2) d_Car^(1/2) (Eq. 4), with fitted slope 97.1 MPa/nm^(1/2) and a flow stress in the absence of κ-carbides of about 478 MPa (Fig. 7a, blocks b0069, b0071); σ_TS ≈ 1350 MPa and σ_FS ≈ 2150 MPa for all investigated compositions (block b0080).

The paper's conclusion (block b0082) states an excellent combination of yield strength 642 MPa, ductility 72% and impact toughness at −40 °C of 247 J at density 6.69 g/cm³ was obtained for Fe30Mn10Al1C after 1050 °C solution treatment; note this toughness value (247 J) differs slightly from the 237 J listed for Al-10 in Table 2 (block b0033).

Charpy impact toughness specimens were cut with the V-notch perpendicular to the rod axis and tested with an MTS impact tester (500 J capacity) at −40 °C (block b0017); impact results are reported for the 1050 °C solution-treated series and no impact data are reported for the 1100 °C state of this sample.
